I finished and wired the schematic together. this took quite a bit because I had to find parts that could connect to each other, and I had to devise a way to make the controllers wireless. I decided on using the pico as the main microcontroller, but esp32c3's as transmitters to connect to the pico wirelessly. the 4 buttons and joystick exist on each side, and everything looks nice :D

### 2026-11-01: finished pcb! routing was actually terrible- I kept having to reroute the area round the IC, and even now it still looks messy. However, its all done!! I just have unconnected lines between my magneti

**6h**

finished pcb! routing was actually terrible- I kept having to reroute the area round the IC, and even now it still looks messy. However, its all done!! I just have unconnected lines between my magnetic pogo connectors and i genuinely can't get rid of those, and also one for 2 isolated copper islands that i'm struggling to solve as well.

### 2026-11-01: wrote the firmware, and updated my repo! I also organized my schematic. I wrote the firmware for the dipado, with the joystick and push button mechanism being written. I wrote it in c++ so that all 3

**5h**

wrote the firmware, and updated my repo! I also organized my schematic. I wrote the firmware for the dipado, with the joystick and push button mechanism being written. I wrote it in c++ so that all 3 microcontrollers can connect to each other!
